question.leadin: Identify these politicians who were powerful during the 1990's.
question.text: This Georgia Republican served as Speaker of the House from 1995 to 1999 and was a co-writer of the Contract with America.
question.clue: This former Speaker of the House from Georgia won the South Carolina primary. During the campaign, he proposed a moon colony that could petition to become a U.S. state.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Republican Presidential hopefuls in the 2012 primary season.
swap.text: After only being allowed to compete in a small number of debates, this former New Mexico governor ran for president with the backing of the Libertarian Party.
swap.clue: This politician was referred to as "Puff Daddy" by Clinton drug czar Barry McCaffrey for his endorsement of marijuana legalization.

question.text: The first Jewish woman to serve on the Supreme Court, she served for 13 years on the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit before being nominated by Bill Clinton in 1993.
question.clue: This co-founder of the ACLU's Women's Rights Project struck down VMI's male-only admission policy as part of her longtime advocacy for women's rights.

swap.leadin: Name the following about politicians who like getting hit in the face.
swap.text: In a charity boxing match, this 2012 Republican U.S. presidential candidate and former governor of Massachusetts lasted two rounds against Evander Holyfield.
swap.clue: This man once claimed he had "binders full of women" and that 47% of Americans would never vote for him.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Supreme Court cases regarding a 2010 piece of legislation.
question.text: In 2013, this art store chain filed a suit against the federal government for requiring they provide insurance that provides contraception, as a violation of their religion rights under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act.
question.clue: This craft store chain that won a 2014 Supreme Court case against the federal government over their opposition to birth control requirements in the Affordable Care Act.

swap.leadin: On July 8, 2013, this man announced that he wouldn't run for governor of Texas, ending his fourteen-year office.
swap.text: Name this governor whose failed 2012 presidential bid was partly blamed on the fact that he wanted to cut the Departments of Commerce, Education, and, um....oops.

question.leadin: This election's eventual winner emerged victorious following the Supreme Court's overturning of a prior ruling requiring a recount in Florida.
question.text: Name this election decided following the Court's ruling in Bush v. Gore.
question.clue: In another state during this election, N. Sanders Sauls became involved in the contest phase of the election after Katherine Harris ended the protest phase.

swap.leadin: This man was the former Mayor of Burlington.
swap.text: Name this Vermont Senator and candidate for the Democratic presidential nomination. He calls himself a "democratic socialist," but had been an Independent prior to caucusing as a Democrat.
swap.clue: This man's campaigns discourage the use of money from Super PACs.

question.text: Odierno assumed command of Iraq's Multi-National Force after this Four Star General, who holds a doctorate from Princeton, became head of U.S. Central Command in October 2008. He was the subject of a controversial 2007 ad placed in the New York Times by MoveOn.org.
question.clue: This man handed control to General Odierno of the Iraq troop surge so he could succeed a man who gave an interview with Rolling Stone, Stanley McChrystal, as commander of NATO forces in Afghanistan.

swap.leadin: This man was tapped for his highest post while serving as President of Texas A&M.
swap.text: Name this man, the only cabinet member from the Bush administration who joined the Obama cabinet. He wrote the tell-all memoir Duty about his time serving both presidents.
swap.clue: In another position held by this man, he dealt with the fallout following a Washington Post article detailing conditions at Walter Reed Medical Center and oversaw a 2007 troop surge.

question.leadin: An early photo of this man shows him standing next to a sign that says "Food for Thought" while volunteering at a Festival of Books.
question.text: Identify this man, who now looks slightly more insane in photos. He has been charged with a mass shooting in Tucson, Arizona, that left six dead and severely injured Representative Gabrielle Giffords.

swap.text: During the 1964 election, this conservative wrote the pro-Goldwater book A Choice, Not an Echo. This activist founded the Eagle Forum and was noted for her opposition to the Equal Rights Amendment.
swap.clue: This person likened "using an atomic bomb to exterminate mice" to legislation sponsored by Michigan representative Martha Griffiths.

question.text: This Solicitor General was instructed by Nixon to fire Cox, and he actually did it. Nominated to the Supreme Court by Reagan, he has since published books like Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern Liberalism and American Decline.
question.clue: This man, who complied in firing Archibald Cox during the Saturday Night Massacre, was the focus of a committee hearing, led by Joe Biden, that decided not to replace Lewis Powell with this man.

swap.leadin: Identify the following now-former members of George W. Bush's staff following their recent resignations.
swap.text: This man succeeded Scott McClellan as the third White House press secretary for George W. Bush. He was accused of insulting the press's intelligence when using the word "nuance" to talk about the commutation of Scooter Libby.

question.leadin: Name some people who, as of the writing of this bonus in early October, were Republican candidates for President.
question.text: This Senator, who is widely rumored to be gay, has remained low in the polls but was widely regarded as the winner of the September 16th "kid's table" debate.
question.clue: In a tweet, this South Carolina senator stated that "any policy proposal which drives up costs of Corona, tequila, or margaritas is a big-time bad idea" in response to a 20% income tax with Mexico to pay the wall.

swap.leadin: Name some winners of 2014 midterm elections.
swap.text: This Republican Kansas governor was re-elected despite more than a hundred Republicans endorsing his Democratic opponent in response to this man's extensive, revenue-negative tax cuts.
swap.clue: This senator from Kansas is a total redneck who advocates complete banning of abortion and a flat tax, and wants to "renew the family".

question.leadin: Identify the following Attorneys-General that all happened to have been the second to serve under their respective presidents.
question.text: This man resigned during the Wedtech scandal, when it was revealed that he did lobbying work for the namesake company. He succeeded William French Smith and has remained active in the Heritage Foundation and Federalist Society.

swap.leadin: A 1988 case brought by this man ruled that public figures were not entitled to emotional damages from parodies that could not reasonably be taken to be factual.
swap.text: This co-founder of the Moral Majority was parodied by Hustler as an incestuous drunkard.
swap.clue: A prominent figure in the Moral Majority was this Baptist minister who established Liberty University in Virginia. This televangelist from the Thomas Road Baptist Church blamed the 9/11 attacks on pagans, feminists and the ACLU.

question.text: This political advocacy group split off from Citizens for a Sound Economy in 2004. Obama named it as one of the "shadowy groups with harmless sounding names," and its agents were criticized for plastering fake eviction notices on Detroit homes in June of 2011.

swap.leadin: The winning candidate in this election made such bloopers as saying that Pearl Harbor occurred on September 7 and that he stood for "anti-Semitism." Answer the following about the election of 1988.
swap.text: Possibly the most exciting moment in the campaign occurred in the vice-presidential debates when this Dukakis running mate and Texas Senator sneered that Dan Quayle was "no Jack Kennedy."
swap.clue: He became president of Lincoln Consolidated during a fifteen-year absence from politics, which ended when he defeated George Bush in a 1970 election for senator from Texas.
